react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent enrichment paradigms converge on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant perturbed pathway in this dataset. RaMP multi-database ORA ranks KEGG:map00380 'Tryptophan metabolism' as the top hit (FDR = 1.5 × 10⁻¹⁴, fold enrichment 667×, 6 metabolites hit) and WikiPathways WP:WP465 'Tryptophan metabolism' rank 3 (FDR = 1.3 × 10⁻¹¹, 5 metabolites hit). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently scores hsa00380 'Tryptophan metabolism' as the top KEGG pathway (p = 1.03 × 10⁻⁶, 5 metabolites hit). Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis returns MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism as rank 0 (p = 0.0021, 12 matched features against a 13-compound pathway module). This four-way convergence — across ORA, PSEA, and m/z network paradigms — establishes tryptophan catabolism as the affected biological process. The driver metabolites span two branches of the pathway: the serotonin-melatonin arm (L-tryptophan → serotonin → melatonin; confirmed in REACT:R-HSA-209931, FDR = 3.5 × 10⁻⁸) and the kynurenine-NAD⁺ arm (L-tryptophan → quinolinic acid → 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid; confirmed in WP:WP4210, WP:WP2485, and WP:WP3645 with fold enrichments >700×). Putrescine and 3-sulfino-L-alanine extend the signal to polyamine metabolism and the cysteine/methionine interface. L-Leucine is a secondary hit consistent with branched-chain amino acid catabolism but does not drive the primary signal.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent enrichment paradigms converge on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant perturbed pathway in this dataset. RaMP multi-database ORA ranks KEGG:map00380 'Tryptophan metabolism' as the top hit (FDR = 1.5 × 10⁻¹⁴, fold enrichment 667×, 6 metabolites hit) and WikiPathways WP:WP465 'Tryptophan metabolism' rank 3 (FDR = 1.3 × 10⁻¹¹, 5 metabolites hit). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently scores hsa00380 'Tryptophan metabolism' as the top KEGG pathway (p = 1.03 × 10⁻⁶, 5 metabolites hit). Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis returns MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism as rank 0 (p = 0.0021, 12 matched features against a 13-compound pathway module). This four-way convergence — across ORA, PSEA, and m/z network paradigms — establishes tryptophan catabolism as the affected biological process. The driver metabolites span two branches of the pathway: the serotonin-melatonin arm (L-tryptophan → serotonin → melatonin; confirmed in REACT:R-HSA-209931, FDR = 3.5 × 10⁻⁸) and the kynurenine-NAD⁺ arm (L-tryptophan → quinolinic acid → 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid; confirmed in WP:WP4210, WP:WP2485, and WP:WP3645 with fold enrichments >700×). Putrescine and 3-sulfino-L-alanine extend the signal to polyamine metabolism and the cysteine/methionine interface. L-Leucine is a secondary hit consistent with branched-chain amino acid catabolism but does not drive the primary signal.
